title: Explain technical work simply
lead: Is lesson ke baad tum hosting, domain, speed, SEO ya bug ko non-technical client ko simple English me samjha paoge — bina jargon ke.
description: Week 6 English lesson: explain hosting, domains, speed, security, and bugs in simple English to non-technical clients.

patterns.note: Comparison se client ko turant idea milta hai.
patterns.say: It's like a shop address for your website.
patterns.positive: It's like a shop address for your website.
patterns.negative: It's not like a physical shop.
patterns.question: What is it like?
examples: Hosting is like rent for your website.
Hosting website ke kiraye jaisa hai.
A domain is like your shop's name board.
Domain aapki dukaan ke naam ke board jaisa hai.
patterns.grammar: It's like + noun. Comparison ke liye. Like yahan ‘pasand’ nahi, ‘jaisa’ hai.
patterns.mistake: “It's like to a shop” → “It's like a shop.” like ke baad noun, to nahi.

patterns.note: Feature se client kya kar sakta hai.
patterns.say: This allows you to update the website yourself.
patterns.positive: This allows you to update the website yourself.
patterns.negative: This doesn't allow you to change the design.
patterns.question: What does this allow me to do?
examples: This allows you to add new products.
Isse aap naye products add kar sakte hain.
The panel allows you to change photos.
Panel se aap photos badal sakte hain.
patterns.grammar: allow + person + to + verb. This allows you to... = isse aap kar sakte ho.
patterns.mistake: “This allows you update” → “This allows you to update.” allow ke baad to.

patterns.note: Problem ko seedha noun se bolo.
patterns.say: The problem is the large images.
patterns.positive: The problem is the large images.
patterns.question: What is the problem?
examples: The problem is the old plugin.
Problem purane plugin ki hai.
The problem is the slow server.
Problem slow server ki hai.
patterns.grammar: The problem is + noun/clause. Simple rakho: noun se shuru karo.
patterns.mistake: “The problem is because the images” → “The problem is the images.” because ki zaroorat nahi.

patterns.note: Technical baat ka client ke liye matlab.
patterns.say: It means the page will open faster.
patterns.positive: It means the page will open faster.
patterns.negative: It doesn't mean the website is new.
patterns.question: What does it mean?
examples: It means your site is safe.
Iska matlab aapki site safe hai.
It means Google can read your pages.
Iska matlab Google aapke pages padh sakta hai.
patterns.grammar: mean + noun/clause. It means = iska matlab hai.
patterns.mistake: “It means that is faster” → “It means the page will open faster.” Clear subject rakho.

patterns.note: Abstract baat ko ek real example se jodo.
patterns.say: For example, a customer can pay online.
patterns.positive: For example, a customer can pay online.
patterns.negative: Not every page needs a form.
patterns.question: Can you give an example?
examples: For example, you can change the price in one click.
Jaise, aap ek click me price badal sakte hain.
For example, a new user can sign up in one minute.
Jaise, naya user ek minute me sign up kar sakta hai.
patterns.grammar: For example, + complete sentence. Comma ke baad sentence complete rakho.
patterns.mistake: “For example a customer can pay” → “For example, a customer can pay.” Example ko complete sentence banao.

patterns.note: Client ko dar mat lagne do — kya nahi karna.
patterns.say: You don't need to install anything.
patterns.negative: You don't need to install anything.
patterns.question: Do I need to do anything?
examples: You don't need to learn coding.
Aapko coding seekhne ki zaroorat nahi.
You don't need to call the developer for this.
Iske liye developer ko call karne ki zaroorat nahi.
patterns.grammar: don't need to + base verb = zaroorat nahi. mustn't = mat karo — meaning different hai.
patterns.mistake: “You don't need install” → “You don't need to install.” need to + base verb.

grammarRules: This allows you to update the site.
The problem is the large images.
It means the page will load faster.
For example, you can pay online.
don't need to + base verb (≠ mustn't)
You don't need to install anything.
mistakes: The problem is because the images.
It means the page will open faster.
You don't need to install anything.
For example a customer can pay online
For example, a customer can pay online.

dialogue.context: Shop owner client ko hosting samjha rahe ho. Riya = client. Jargon zero, comparison aur example use karo.

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.text: So why do I need hosting?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Hosting is like rent for your website. The files live on a server.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: The domain is like your shop's name board. It's the address people type.

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.text: Will it be fast? Do I need to learn coding?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes, it will load faster. You don't need to install anything. For example, you can change a photo from your phone.

dialogue.closing: Technical answer se pehle ek comparison do, phir ek example. Client ko rule nahi, result chahiye.

speakPrompts.title: 1. Hosting
speakPrompts.prompt: Hosting ko ek comparison se samjhao.

speakPrompts.title: 2. Domain
speakPrompts.prompt: Domain aur address ka relation batao.
speakPrompts.starter: A domain is like ___ . For example, ___ .

speakPrompts.title: 3. A problem
speakPrompts.prompt: Slow site ka reason simple bolo.

speakPrompts.title: 4. 60-second explanation
speakPrompts.prompt: Ek technical cheez non-technical friend ko samjhao.
speakPrompts.starter: It's like ___ . This allows you to ___ . You don't need to ___ .

vocab.example: Hosting is like rent for your website.
The domain is your site's address.
The site is responsive on mobile.
We take a backup every night.
The plugin adds a contact form.
A new user can sign up in a minute.

selfCheck: Ek technical word ko comparison se samjhaya.
“This allows you to ___” se benefit bataya.
Problem ko “The problem is ___” se seedha bola.
Client ka dar kam kiya — “You don't need to ___”.
60 seconds me jargon ke bina bola.

pronunciation.title: Technical stress
pronunciation.body: HOSTing, doMAIN, reSPONsive, seCURity. Stress ek syllable par, baaki halke.

pronunciation.title: Integration
pronunciation.body: in-te-GRA-tion — stress third syllable par. ‘integration’ ko jaldi bolne ki koshish mat karo.

pronunciation.title: It's like
pronunciation.body: Linking: it's-like = /ɪtslaɪk/. Do words ko jodo, ruk kar mat bolo.

pronunciation.title: Contrast stress
pronunciation.body: The problem is the IMAGES, not the HOSTING. Contrast par stress badalta hai.

followUps: Hosting ko ek line me aur simple kaise samjhaun?
“It's like” ke aur natural comparisons kya hain?
Client ko jargon se bachne ka rule kya hai?
Mera explanation 60 seconds me fit hai?
“You don't need to” ka tone confident lagta hai?
mission: Explain one technical thing to a non-technical friend in 60 seconds — ek comparison, ek example, zero jargon.

source.label: BBC Learning English · 6 Minute English
source.note: Technology wala episode chuno. Target: do simple explanation phrases note karna.

Simple shabdon me, ye tez hai.
